description: Somos SpaceTech UTC, un equipo de cinco estudiantes de Ingeniería de Sistemas apasionados por la arquitectura de software, el desarrollo de sistemas embebidos, la telemática y la gestión de datos críticos. Nuestro fuerte radica en diseñar soluciones tecnológicas resilientes, optimizar código bajo entornos de recursos limitados y analizar sistemas complejos de alta tolerancia a fallos, donde aplicaremos nuestra visión de ingeniería inversa y análisis de sistemas para explorar.
summary:
We developed an interactive educational website designed for everyone interested in learning, discovering, and exploring more about space exploration. Our project aims to give a voice to the equipment and artifacts left behind on the Moon and Mars after completing their missions.

Through 3D globes, real NASA textures, coordinates, and data from the official NSSDCA catalog, users can explore different missions and learn the stories behind each artifact. Additionally, we incorporated Spanish narrations, synchronized subtitles, a frequency-tuning minigame, trivia challenges, and achievement badges that transform learning into an interactive and entertaining experience.

ECHOES OF SOL addresses the challenge by transforming abandoned space equipment into the protagonists of stories that connect science, technology, and emotion. It is important because it helps people understand that these artifacts are not simply space debris, but rather testimonies of human exploration that deserve to be remembered. We aim to spark curiosity, encourage learning, and make knowledge about space accessible to everyone.
details:
Project Details – ECHOES OF SOL

ECHOES OF SOL is an interactive educational web platform designed to bring back the stories of the space equipment and artifacts left behind on the Moon and Mars after completing their missions. Our project transforms these objects into the protagonists of an experience focused on exploration, learning, and discovery.

What does it do and how does it work?

The platform allows users to explore three-dimensional globes of Mars and the Moon, using real NASA textures and markers representing the locations of different space artifacts. By selecting one of them, users can access an information card containing its coordinates, important dates, last transmission, and scientific legacy, using information obtained from official NASA sources, especially the NSSDCA catalog.

Additionally, we incorporated a first-person storytelling system in which each artifact tells its story through Spanish audio narrations and word-by-word synchronized subtitles. We also developed a frequency-tuning minigame, trivia challenges, and achievement badges that turn space exploration into an engaging and interactive experience.

What are its benefits and expected impact?

Our project is designed for anyone interested in learning about space exploration, regardless of age or level of knowledge. It aims to bring science and technology closer to the public through an educational experience in Spanish, accessible directly from a web browser without requiring software installation.

Its expected impact is to spark scientific curiosity, strengthen interactive learning, and raise awareness of the historical and scientific value of the artifacts that remain on other worlds. We want to demonstrate that they are not simply space debris, but rather testimonies of humanity's progress, efforts, and discoveries.

What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed the project using web technologies:

  • HTML5 to structure the platform.
  • CSS3 for the visual design and interface inspired by space exploration systems.
  • JavaScript for application logic and interactions.
  • Three.js to render three-dimensional globes of Mars and the Moon.
  • GSAP to implement interactive narrative scrolling (scrollytelling).
  • Web Audio API for sound experiences.
  • Web Components to create reusable components using the custom echo-* element family.
  • JSON and the NSSDCA catalog to organize and display mission data.
  • Edge-TTS with the es-EC-LuisNeural voice to generate Spanish narrations and synchronized subtitles.
  • localStorage to save achievement badges and user progress.

The prototype runs entirely on the frontend, without its own server or database, reducing infrastructure costs and making it easy to access through a web browser.

What makes our project creative and innovative?

Our main innovation is transforming scientific and historical information into an interactive storytelling experience. Instead of presenting only technical data, we allow the artifacts to tell their stories in the first person, as if their final transmissions could once again be heard from Earth.

We combine 3D visualization, audio storytelling, geographical exploration, and gamification to create an emotional connection between the public and the history of space exploration.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered accessibility, language, ease of use, development costs, information accuracy, and audience diversity. For these reasons, we designed an experience in Spanish that runs directly in a web browser and requires neither software installation nor dedicated server infrastructure. We also prioritized the use of data and textures from official NASA sources to provide reliable information.

ECHOES OF SOL is our first functional prototype and represents a step toward a more complete educational experience. As a future development stage, we plan to migrate the data to Supabase to implement a real API and enable users to save their progress.
